Complete case study: fishery survey catch-composition data

Source: vignettes/articles/case-study-survey-catch.Rmd
case-study-survey-catch.Rmd

Why use DietView for survey catches?

A catch matrix is not a predator diet, but it still describes the composition of identified taxa within a sampling unit. This complete simulated exercise starts with hauls as rows and taxa as columns, passes through an explicit checked taxonomy, and ends with a hierarchical figure, haul-occurrence table, sample matrix and optional HTML dashboard.

Question: What proportion of the recorded catch mass belongs to each taxon in this synthetic haul survey, and which taxa are unidentified?

Unit: one haul. Quantity: catch mass in kg. Pseudo-predator role: a constant label "Survey catch" required by the DietView API; it is not an organism. Stratum: survey region. The output is a description of captured material, not an estimate of fish abundance or feeding.

Construct and inspect the sample frame 

library(DietView)
set.seed(640)
hauls <- data.frame(haul_id = sprintf("H%02d", 1:24),
                    region = rep(c("North", "South"), each = 12),
                    vessel = rep(c("V1", "V2"), 12))
hauls$assemblage <- "Survey catch"
# Use one haul as a known zero-catch sample, retained in the inventory.
make_w <- function(n, rate) round(stats::rgamma(n, shape = 2, rate = rate), 2)
wide <- data.frame(
  haul_id = hauls$haul_id, region = hauls$region,
  `Gadus morhua` = make_w(24, 0.22),
  `Clupea harengus` = make_w(24, 0.15),
  `Crangon crangon` = make_w(24, 0.45),
  `Unidentified fish` = make_w(24, 1.1),
  check.names = FALSE
)
wide[1, setdiff(names(wide), c("haul_id", "region"))] <- 0
hauls$empty <- rowSums(wide[setdiff(names(wide), c("haul_id", "region"))]) == 0
head(wide)
#>   haul_id region Gadus morhua Clupea harengus Crangon crangon Unidentified fish
#> 1     H01  North         0.00            0.00            0.00              0.00
#> 2     H02  North        12.04            9.10            5.51              4.00
#> 3     H03  North         9.00           15.14            6.50              1.90
#> 4     H04  North        20.69           15.46            2.30              0.40
#> 5     H05  North         4.75            4.03            4.61              4.43
#> 6     H06  North        12.19            8.44            6.87              3.01

The sample-frame table holds all 24 hauls. The wide matrix contains one mass value per haul and taxon. In a real survey, add tow duration, swept area, gear, vessel, habitat and sampling strata; retain reasons for missing values rather than converting all missing measurements to zero.

taxa <- setdiff(names(wide), c("haul_id", "region"))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(hauls$haul_id))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(as.matrix(wide[taxa]))),
          all(as.matrix(wide[taxa]) >= 0))
c(hauls = nrow(hauls), zeros = sum(hauls$empty),
  total_kg = sum(as.matrix(wide[taxa])))
#>    hauls    zeros total_kg 
#>    24.00     1.00   744.61

Convert wide data to the required long format 

long <- dv_from_wide(wide, taxa_in = "columns",
                     id_cols = c("haul_id", "region"),
                     sample_col = "haul_id", value_col = "catch_kg",
                     taxon_col = "prey_name")
long$assemblage <- "Survey catch"
head(long[, c("haul_id", "region", "prey_name", "catch_kg")])
#>   haul_id region    prey_name catch_kg
#> 1     H02  North Gadus morhua    12.04
#> 2     H03  North Gadus morhua     9.00
#> 3     H04  North Gadus morhua    20.69
#> 4     H05  North Gadus morhua     4.75
#> 5     H06  North Gadus morhua    12.19
#> 6     H07  North Gadus morhua     5.75
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sum(long$catch_kg), sum(as.matrix(wide[taxa])))))

The variable name prey_name is inherited from DietView’s diet-focused interface. These taxa are catch components, not prey. Zeros were dropped as absent taxon–haul records; the zero-catch haul remains in hauls.

Attach a frozen taxonomy and retain coarse identifications

For a real survey, source this classification from a checked WoRMS/GBIF release and archive its identifiers and date. Here it is explicitly illustrative, with one deliberately unidentified fish category.

lineage <- data.frame(
  prey_name = c("Gadus morhua", "Clupea harengus", "Crangon crangon",
                "Unidentified fish"),
  kingdom = rep("Animalia", 4),
  phylum = c("Chordata", "Chordata", "Arthropoda", "Chordata"),
  class = c("Actinopteri", "Actinopteri", "Malacostraca", "Actinopteri"),
  order = c("Gadiformes", "Clupeiformes", "Decapoda", NA),
  family = c("Gadidae", "Clupeidae", "Crangonidae", NA),
  genus = c("Gadus", "Clupea", "Crangon", NA),
  species = c("Gadus morhua", "Clupea harengus", "Crangon crangon", NA)
)
spec <- dv_spec(predator = "assemblage", stomach = "haul_id",
                prey_name = "prey_name", weight = "catch_kg",
                weight_type = "mass", unit_label = "haul",
                covariates = "region")
prep <- dv_prepare(long, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = lineage,
                   stomachs = hauls, empty_col = "empty", verbose = FALSE)
prep
#> <dietview_prep>
#>   records   : 92 
#>   hauls     : 23 
#>   predators : 1 
#>   ranks     : kingdom > phylum > class > order > family > genus > species 
#>   covariates: region 
#>   source    : table 
#>   examined  : 24 hauls, 1 empty

Calculate mass composition and haul occurrence 

tree <- dv_tree(prep)
phylum <- dv_rank_table(tree, "Phylum")
phylum[, c("label", "value_w", "pct_w", "pct_occ")]
#>        label value_w    pct_w pct_occ
#> 3   Chordata  643.17 86.37676      75
#> 2 Arthropoda  101.44 13.62324      25
fo <- dv_fo_table(prep, rank = "class", denominator = "examined")
fo[, c("taxon", "n_stomachs", "n_total", "pct_fo")]
#>          taxon n_stomachs n_total pct_fo
#> 1  Actinopteri         23      24  95.83
#> 2 Malacostraca         23      24  95.83

value_w is kg of recorded catch and pct_w the percentage of total recorded catch mass. pct_occ is the proportion of non-zero taxon–haul records; it is not the relative number of fish. pct_fo is the percentage of examined hauls with recorded catches of a category (a presence frequency), not the diet frequency of occurrence of any predator.

A large mass share can reflect a few large hauls. It must not be interpreted as stock biomass, population abundance, CPUE or habitat preference without sampling effort, catchability and survey-design adjustments.

dv_sunburst(tree, mode = "weight", title = "Simulated survey catch",
            subtitle = "Share of recorded catch mass (kg); not predator diet")

White wedges below the classified fish lineage show the mass not identified to order/family/species. Dropping them would spuriously inflate the shares of precisely identified species.

Export a haul-by-taxon matrix with the zero-catch haul 

m <- dv_matrix(prep, rank = "family", currency = "weight",
               include_empty = TRUE)
c(hauls = nrow(m), categories = ncol(m))
#>      hauls categories 
#>         24          4
stopifnot(nrow(m) == nrow(hauls))
head(rowSums(m))
#>   H02   H03   H04   H05   H06   H07 
#> 30.65 32.54 38.85 17.82 30.51 18.52
utils::write.csv(m, file.path(tempdir(), "survey_catch_kg_by_haul.csv"))

For downstream multivariate work, document whether the matrix contains raw kg, kg/hour, kg/swept km², or another effort-standardized quantity. DietView exports raw values; it does not infer survey design or apply catchability corrections.

Optional HTML output and reporting notes 

dv_build_html(prep,
  output = file.path(getwd(), "survey_catch_demo.html"),
  bands = c("occurrence", "weight"), strata = "region",
  title = "Simulated survey catch composition — not a diet")

A scientific report should state the target population, sample selection, tow/gears and effort, units and detection limits, treatment of zero catches, taxonomic authority, reporting rank, uncertainty, and whether estimates are weighted to the survey design. This vignette is a demonstration of a hierarchical composition tool, not a replacement for fisheries stock assessment or ecosystem-survey estimators.
